references.text: The Lord emphasizes that he has announced things beforehand so that they may believe it is the Father who speaks, a theme central to Jesus' argument about doing the Father's will.
The prophet is called to hear and see, and to do God's will, reflecting the contrast between Jesus' obedience and the opponent's unwillingness to hear the Father.
Jesus' own explanation that he does nothing on his own but only what he sees the Father doing is a direct theological parallel to the statement in John 8:38.
Jesus' claim that he has not spoken on his own, but that the Father who sent him gave him both message and commandment, underscores the same source of authority as in John 8:38.
Jesus' assertion that the words he speaks are not his own but the Father's who dwells in him is a direct elaboration of the principle of speaking what one has seen with the Father.
